findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity as primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; recorded affinities are removed and the label prior is equal-score, so no observed affinity outcome is available to score coordinate hypotheses against.

Continuous contrast functions over the observed window are non-monotone: landmark local-coordinate features show multiple sign changes (e.g. 4-10 sign changes) with large first-vs-last rate z-scores of opposite sign, and no polynomial fit is accepted; a constant rule is therefore not supported and any time-conditioned rule must stay within observed-node interpolation, since extrapolation is disallowed.

Joint selection-innovation diagnostics show a coherent positive association of innovation with native alignment (q~2.2e-9, positive batch fraction 1.0) and high teacher-contrast coherence (~0.81), while observed child score gain is negative (q~1.8e-7, positive batch fraction 0.0); this indicates selection enrichment is coupled to alignment/coherence rather than to an absolute geometric descriptor or to observed child quality gain.

hypotheses.direction: time-conditioned contrast aligned to observed-node sign changes
hypotheses.falsifier: No improvement in observed-node contrast fidelity or alignment relative to a constant rule within the observed window.
hypotheses.observable: landmark local-coordinate contrast at observed score nodes
hypotheses.scope: observed window [0.0,0.5], predicted endpoint world-A features
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned coordinate contrast that follows the observed-node sign structure of landmark local-coordinate features (rather than a constant contrast) would better track the observed selection-innovation alignment than a constant rule.

hypotheses.direction: joint coherent pattern over isolated marginals
hypotheses.falsifier: Marginal-only descriptors match or exceed joint-pattern measures on the same diagnostics.
hypotheses.statement: Selection enrichment is driven by coherent joint coordinate patterns (alignment/coherence) rather than isolated marginal descriptors, so a joint-pattern-preserving coordinate reward should outperform marginal-only descriptors.

limitations: No decoded terminal affinity labels or current-study outcome data are supplied; last-record/observed child score gain is not final affinity benefit and cannot be presented as such.
Continuous-trend and joint diagnostics are descriptive associations with batch as the independent unit; they are not causal selection effects, atom velocities, or physical interaction energies.
Temperatures are immutable task parameters and were not proposed for edit; no reward recipe change is asserted here.
Turnover/parent-child increment accounting and survival/last-record joint-head semantics were not read in this pass and remain unassessed.
